audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells you to answer Zac's engage with Aegis Assault — "when he commits an E sling or Q knockback, pop E to block the directional damage", and wants.you[1] "Bait his E sling/Q knockback into your E block".
audit.why: Aegis Assault is a channel and every displacement in Zac's kit — Stretching Strikes, Elastic Slingshot and Let's Bounce! all carry knockup — cancels it outright. Riot's own text is "becoming invulnerable to damage from the front", so it is directional as well, not a bubble. A Pantheon told to raise E into the slingshot loses an 80-mana 22s cooldown for nothing and eats the full combo. The correct instruction is the opposite: spend Aegis Assault on his poke and answer the engage with the Shield Vault stun.
audit.corrected: Aegis Assault turns away damage from the front only, and any Zac knockup cancels the channel — E his poke, W his engage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstable Matter is never mentioned, and Cell Division is described only as "blobs" to step on — Grievous Wounds never appears in the content layer.
audit.why: Unstable Matter deals a percentage of your maximum health as magic damage on a 5-second cooldown, so it repeats inside every extended trade and stacking armour does nothing against it. Cell Division sheds chunks that heal him when reabsorbed, which is exactly what Grievous Wounds is for. Both are the mechanical reason the 2+ item stage flips, and neither reached the page even though the full layer already buys Executioner's Calling.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter is max-health magic damage every 5s; Cell Division chunks heal him back — carry anti-heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Elastic Slingshot is named in nine places as "his engage" and never once given a number.
audit.why: It is 21/18/15/12/9s while your Shield Vault is 13/12/11/10/9s. That single comparison is the whole lane: at rank 1 you get roughly eight seconds after he spends it where your engage is up and his is not. "Bait it" without the numbers is advice a player cannot act on; the numbers turn it into a clock.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot 21s at rank 1 vs Shield Vault 13s — that gap is your window.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why and breakdown.early both open "Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright."
audit.why: Pantheon has no passive shield. Mortal Will is "Every few spells or attacks, Pantheon's next spell is empowered" — an empowerment, not a shield. The shield in this matchup is Aegis Assault, a separate 22s ability, and conflating them makes a player expect free mitigation at level 1 that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Mortal Will empowers every third cast; there is no passive shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] read [Skill, Pantheon, Pantheon, Skill, Skill, Pantheon, Pantheon] — Pantheon holding both item stages against a matchup Zac reclaims.
audit.why: The packet levelChart gives Pantheon the first six stages and Zac the last, and the mirror audit at audits/top/zac__pantheon.json settled the same chart from Zac's side: Pantheon levels 1-6, Skill at first item, Zac at 2+ items. The entry's own whys[6] already says Zac reclaims the lane while win[6] said Pantheon — the two contradicted each other on the same row. Aligning win[] to the mirror fixes that and keeps the two directions from fighting.
audit.corrected: Pantheon levels 1 through 6, Skill at first item, Zac at 2+ items.

audit.why: The core trading instruction — fight early, W-stun into empowered Q, do not let the lane reach two items — matches the kits and the 612-game record. Only the Aegis Assault half of it was wrong, corrected above.

The full layer already lists Executioner's Calling early against Cell Division sustain. That is the right call and the right timing; the content layer simply never echoed it, which the early-paragraph edit fixes.

edits.before: Zac is an off-meta tank with no real level 1 — your point-and-click W stun and its damage make you one of the strongest champs on the map here, so look to fight the moment you can reach him. He has no escape until his E charges, so a level 2-3 W-stun into empowered Q and an E channel out-trades him cleanly. The one thing that undoes you is letting him walk over the four blobs his passive drops on the ground after spells — deny those by fighting on top of him or pushing him off them.
edits.after: Zac is an off-meta tank with no real level 1 — your point-and-click W stun and its damage make you one of the strongest champs on the map here, so fight the moment you can reach him. His only engage, Elastic Slingshot, is 21s at rank 1 while your Shield Vault is 13s, so you get a free window every time he spends it. What undoes you is letting him reabsorb the four Cell Division chunks he sheds after spells — deny those by fighting on top of him, and buy Executioner's Calling once trades go long.

edits.before: This is your takeover window. Hold-and-aim your Q from max range to chunk him as he tries to last-hit, and when he commits an E sling or Q knockback, pop E to block the directional damage and immediately W-stun back into him. At 6, Grand Starfall is your roam button more than a 1v1 finisher — use your lane lead to leap bot or mid and snowball the map while Zac is stuck farming and can't punish your absence.
edits.after: This is your takeover window. Hold-and-aim your Q from max range to chunk him as he tries to last-hit. Aegis Assault only turns away damage from the front and any knockup cancels the channel, so raise it against his poke and answer his engage with the W-stun instead. At 6, Grand Starfall is your roam button more than a 1v1 finisher — leap bot or mid and snowball the map while Zac farms and can't punish your absence.

edits.before: Zac flips the script hard at 2+ items. He stacks raw tank stats, his Cell Division passive makes him functionally unkillable as long as he grabs blobs, and his double E sling plus Q/W CC let him peel and disrupt while your damage plateaus. Do not try to 1v1 a fed full-tank Zac — close the game on your accumulated lead before then, or kite his engage and let your carries handle the front line.
edits.after: Zac flips the script hard at 2+ items. Unstable Matter takes a share of your max health every 5s, Cell Division feeds it straight back, and his passive revives him outright on a 5-minute cooldown — stacking armour answers none of that. Do not 1v1 a fed full-tank Zac: close on your accumulated lead first, or dodge Let's Bounce! and let your carries handle the front line.
